title: Contractor Invoice Template: Construction Billing in PDF, Word, Excel
description: Bill construction and remodeling work from your browser: progress payments, change orders, deposits. No sign-up. PDF, Word and Excel, with sourced US prices.
lede_html: Use this form for general contractor and construction jobs, then download a PDF, Word or Excel file. You need no account. The sample is a second progress bill on a kitchen. Replace it.

must_show.heading: What a contractor invoice must show
must_show.intro_html: A construction invoice links the amount to the contract: which stage, which change order, what the customer already paid, and what remains.
must_show.why_label: Why it matters on a construction job
rows: Lets the owner check your license. California asks for it on the contract.
One job can have many bills, so give each one a reference.
Name the stage reached, for example rough-in passed.
Each one gets its own line with its number and date.
The form prints what the customer paid and the balance.

rules.heading: Contractor rules that touch the invoice

items.title: Down payment cap in California
items.html: On home improvement jobs, the down payment cannot pass the lesser of $1,000 or 10 percent, except for blanket-bond licensees. Later payments cannot exceed the value of work performed.

items.title: Change orders in writing
items.html: The California CSLB guide says that a price change must be a written change order in the contract. New Jersey requires written changes to home improvement contracts over $500.

items.title: Lien rights
items.html: In California, suppliers and subcontractors give the owner a Preliminary Notice within 20 days of delivering material or starting work. Contractors give a Mechanics Lien Warning.

faq.q: How do I bill a progress payment?
faq.a: Enter one line per stage with quantity 1. Put the stage in the description, enter past payments in the form, and the file prints the balance due.

faq.q: Is this form for a 1099 independent contractor?
faq.a: Yes. A self-employed person who bills a business can use it. Use the freelancer page if you bill by hours or by project with no parts.

faq.q: Should each change order have its own invoice?
faq.a: It can. Most jobs add a line to the next progress bill with the change order number, so one document shows the running total.

faq.q: Can I bill for material that is on site but not installed?
faq.a: Your contract decides this. In California, payments cannot exceed the value of the performed work, so check this before you bill material that is not installed.
